name: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome due to 11p15 Translocation/Inversion

criteria.description: Abdominal wall defects such as omphalocele or umbilical hernia
Molecular confirmation of 11p15 translocation or inversion affecting imprinting centers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Molecular confirmation of 11p15 translocation/inversion plus at least one major clinical feature
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing due to phenotypic overlap with other BWS causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic enlarged tongue causing feeding and respiratory difficulties
Asymmetric overgrowth of one side of the body or limbs
searchTerms: one side of body larger than the other

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal wall defects (Omphalocele or Umbilical Hernia)
pathognomonic.notes: Midline defects of the abdominal wall present at birth
searchTerms: abdominal wall defect with organ protrusion

common.notes: Low blood sugar in the neonatal period requiring treatment
Characteristic ear anomalies including creases or preauricular pits
searchTerms: folds or pits on outer ear
ear creases or small indentations near ear

common.notes: Enlargement of organs such as liver, kidneys, or pancreas
searchTerms: big liver, spleen, or other organs

occasional.notes: Increased risk of embryonal kidney tumor
Rare liver tumor associated with BWS
Enlargement of the heart observed in some cases

searchTerms: too much amniotic fluid in pregnancy
excess fluid around fetus before birth

rare.symptomName: Neonatal respiratory distress due to macroglossia
searchTerms: breathing difficulty in newborn due to large tongue

laboratory: Neonatal hypoglycemia with elevated insulin levels
Abnormal serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels in tumor surveillance
imaging: Ultrasound showing organomegaly and abdominal wall defects
MRI or CT for tumor detection (Wilms tumor, hepatoblastoma)
genetic: Detection of 11p15 chromosomal translocation or inversion affecting imprinting centers IC1 or IC2
Loss of imprinting or methylation abnormalities at 11p15 locus
other: Clinical examination revealing macroglossia and hemihyperplasia
Prenatal ultrasound findings of macrosomia and polyhydramnios

distinguishingFeatures: Macroglossia without abdominal wall defects or hemihyperplasia
Overgrowth syndrome with distinct facial features

redFlags: Rapid abdominal mass growth suggestive of Wilms tumor
Persistent neonatal hypoglycemia unresponsive to standard treatment
Severe airway obstruction due to macroglossia
references: Weksberg R, Shuman C, Beckwith JB. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Eur J Hum Genet. 2010;18(1):8-14.
Brioude F, et al. Expert consensus document: Clinical and molecular diagnosis, screening and management of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2018;14(4):229-249.
Orphanet: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome due to 11p15 translocation/inversion. ORPHA:231130.
